source.title: Simple and Effective Regularization Methods for Training on Noisily Labeled Data with Generalization Guarantee
source.authors: Wei Hu; Zhiyuan Li; Ding-Li Yu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how test performance changes under increasing label corruption using regularized training methods, but does not test fitting a completely random labeling or the original unregularized setup.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) for fitting arbitrary labels; that cited result is not this study's result. Its own experiments corrupt labels at rates up to 0.6 and report test accuracy. The training curves are figure-only; the text does not state that training error reaches zero.
record.test_reason: The normal-training baselines test V4's test-error degradation component across label-corruption rates 0–0.6. They report validation-selected test accuracy, however, and do not establish perfect training fit. AUX results chiefly evaluate the authors' mitigation method.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors prove clean-distribution generalization bounds for RDI and AUX in sufficiently wide networks under NTK assumptions, and empirically find performance comparable to or better than early stopping. Their empirical effectiveness for ResNet-34 outside the likely NTK regime remains theoretically unexplained.
record.recipe_differences: Uses label corruption and regularization methods (distance-to-initialization and auxiliary variables), with experiments reporting test performance; does not reproduce the original random-label fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy differs by training method and loss (Table 1); AUX results are reported at last and best epochs. The paper also notes a discrepancy between SGD+AUX and SGD+RDI in binary CIFAR, possibly due to SGD noise or finite width.

fits_no_version.finding: AUX improves noisy-label test accuracy and makes last-epoch performance close to best-epoch performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-example auxiliary variables can improve generalization under label corruption without requiring early stopping.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 experiment reports test accuracy, not training error; the paper says the ResNet-34 is likely outside the NTK regime. Results for MNIST and binary CIFAR are figures, and the detailed plotted values are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also plots Setting 1 MNIST test error versus noise rate and Setting 2 binary CIFAR training and test errors at noise rate 20% (Figure 1); these figure-only points are not extracted because the CIFAR-10 table provides numerical results across corruption rates and the figures' plotted values are not stated in text.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Training-time ratios for true versus random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit at each corruption rate, the completely random-label endpoint, and simultaneous signal learning and noise memorization. CIFAR-10 corruption replaces labels with a different class, so its corruption fraction is not identical to uniform random relabeling.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing these methods preserves clean-label generalization.
Direct comparison of learning trajectories for correctly and incorrectly labeled examples. Early-stopping effectiveness and little early overfitting do not establish their learning order.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 values and model attribution match the supplied text. Figure 2 reports test accuracy during training, not training accuracy. Figures 1 and 5 are already declared in rows_left_out; their curve values cannot be reconstructed reliably from this text. AUX training error in those figures includes auxiliary variables and cannot establish memorization by the network alone.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment tests completely random labels with the original architecture and training hyperparameters, or reports chance test error under that condition.
No comparison measures training time for true versus random labels or convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.

Tests test accuracy under label corruption only through noise rate 0.6; does not test all labels corrupted, establish perfect training fit at each rate, or show that the network captures remaining signal while memorizing noise.
Does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Does not measure the order in which real-label patterns and noisy labels are learned over training.
